body.target_estimand: \(\bigl(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R),\;\mathcal G_{\mathrm{cov}}(\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K})\setminus\mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R)\bigr)\) modulo the common monomial action \(\mathfrak M_q\).
body.estimand_functional: \(\bigl(\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K}\bigr)\longmapsto\bigl(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R),\;\mathcal G_{\mathrm{cov}}(\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K})\setminus\mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R)\bigr)/\mathfrak M_q\), with the soft set evaluated by actual-row terminal and affine certificates and covariance membership evaluated pointwise by a legal positive-real realization.

sampling_model.design: Population structure identification from one baseline and one unknown-target single-node soft-intervention context per latent node. The terminal actual-row theorem covers \(2\le p\le q\); the pointwise covariance separation is the worked noninjective case \(p=2,q=4\).
sampling_model.units: Inputs are the aligned population factorization datum \(\mathcal R\) and, for pointwise covariance comparison, the \(q+1\) population covariance matrices \(\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K}\). There is no finite-sample claim.
sampling_model.treatment: Each non-source context changes every incoming coefficient of one latent target and retains every changed edge. Graphs and certificates are identified only modulo one common latent permutation and nonzero diagonal scaling.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition applies. All error variances are positive. Terminal compatibility also permits \(t_k=v_k\); the worked fork pointwise family assumes \(T>0\), \(T\ne1\). Chamberwise covariance claims, where discussed diagnostically, retain both signs of true variance change and permit variance-neutral candidate twins.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Aligned factor directions and source laws modulo common monomial action are population inputs. Recovery from raw laws, finite-sample cumulant estimation, and uniform statistical error control are outside scope.

body.tldr: The headline is now exact and pointwise. Actual soft-intervention rows \(h_k^{\mathsf T}=\delta_k^{\mathsf T}(I_q-\Lambda^{(0)})^{-1}\) admit a sound-and-complete terminal-copy linkage and batched affine-support test in \(O(q^4)\) rational-function field operations. Definition 3.14 of Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal remains the published baseline-path class; the four-node determinant \(\gamma(\beta d-b\delta)\) shows that Theorem 3.15 incorrectly identifies it with actual-row compatibility. For every \(T>0\), \(T\ne1\), the worked \(p=2,q=4\) fork datum has a quotient-invariant pointwise covariance realization by \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\) but the actual-row obstruction \(-2\) excludes that graph from the pointwise soft set. This does not prove chamberwise density or \(\mathsf{Frontier}_2\) membership. The all-branch positive-real compiler remains open.

project_justification.gap: Equation (20) of Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal uses the actual inverse-update rows, while Definition 3.14 deliberately records a baseline inverse-path class. The gap is in Theorem 3.15's identification of those two rank systems: specializing independent intervention changes to baseline coefficients can lower an augmented rank. Problem 5.2 poses a separate covariance-versus-higher-cumulant question, but neither the fork chamberwise density alternative nor a graph-specific non-quantifier-elimination criterion is established.
project_justification.niche: The contribution separates three levels that had been conflated: exact actual-row graph compatibility, quotient-invariant pointwise observable covariance separation, and robust chamberwise covariance density. Terminal-copy linkage plus one batched affine reduction per candidate column completely solves the first. The rational fork family and its \(-2\) affine inconsistency solve a concrete pointwise instance of the second. The third remains an explicitly delimited projection problem.
project_justification.fill: The paper delivers the corrected \(O(q^4)\) terminal algorithm, an exact finite comparison with the unchanged Definition 3.14 class, an anchor-domain counterexample to Theorem 3.15, and the pointwise fork covariance-minus-soft graph witness modulo common sign, scale, and permutation action. Covariance factor branches and the eight-system fork reduction remain secondary diagnostics. No chamberwise dense cover, full-dimensional separator, all-pair compiler, pathwidth guarantee, coefficient-height bound, or infinite generic-strictness family is claimed.

body.related_work: Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (2025) provide the recovery anchor in Theorem 1.7, derive the actual intervention-row equations in Equation (20), define the baseline inverse-path class in Definition 3.14, identify those systems in Theorem 3.15, and pose compatible-graph and covariance-versus-higher-cumulant questions in Problems 5.1--5.2. The present correction preserves Definition 3.14 and refutes only the unsupported identification in Theorem 3.15. Squires, Seigal, Bhate, and Uhler (2023) recover transitive-closure information for injective soft-intervention models; that result does not decide the noninjective positive-real projection here. Half-trek, semidefinite realization, affine-birational, and tree-accelerated elimination results remain methodological context rather than claimed solutions to the open branch-union problem.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The complete regular fork fiber is reduced to eight legal two-scalar positive systems, but their projected union has not been classified over the full true parameter domain. The prescribed fixed resultant and subresultant attempt retained all true coordinates as parameters and eliminated only the two candidate scalars; it failed before emitting projection polynomials, sign cells, or Thom-encoded sample certificates. The rational \(T\)-family, positive candidate variances \(T+144/121\) and \(19/4\), exact five-covariance verification, the obstruction \(-2\), and audited Jacobian regularity establish pointwise feasibility and local facts only. They cannot certify chamberwise density or a full-dimensional separator.
body.honest_scope: The corrected terminal theorem is exact on its declared generic coefficient locus, independent of variance activity, and has an \(O(q^4)\) arithmetic-field bound with no expanded bit-complexity claim. Its finite Definition 3.14 agreement procedure may enumerate same-closure DAGs, so no polynomial total graph-enumeration bound is asserted. The anchor transfer is one-way: the exact-change retained-edge counterexample lies inside the published generic soft domain and therefore refutes a superclass theorem, while positive subclass results do not automatically extend upward. The fork corollary is quotient-invariant and pointwise; it explicitly does not establish \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\in\mathsf{Frontier}_2(G_{\mathrm{fork}})\). The all-chamber fork density test, dense-cover or separator certificates, all-pair non-quantifier-elimination compiler, complexity and pathwidth bounds, and infinite equality or generic-strictness families remain open.
body.interpretation: At population level the companion LCD workflow can now return the corrected actual-row compatible DAG set and, for each accepted or rejected candidate, a terminal linkage or cut, an affine inconsistency, an identically-zero support form, or an avoiding-point certificate. For the worked fork datum it can additionally report a genuine pointwise covariance alternative: the candidate reproduces all five covariances but cannot reproduce the aligned soft-intervention factor datum, and this verdict is invariant to sign, scale, and permutation representatives. It must label that conclusion pointwise. Higher cumulants remove this displayed covariance alternative, but whether they remove covariance alternatives generically across each full-dimensional chamber remains unresolved.
